tagline.text: A tiny coral island and sea turtle sanctuary off Camiguin's east coast

location.label: Location
location.text: Off Mahinog, Camiguin (about 3.5 km from the coast)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half day (up to about 3 hours on the island)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,300 (per person, with a shared boat and snorkeling)

children.text: Mantigue Island is a small coral island of about 4 hectares off Mahinog in Camiguin, managed by the local government as a sea turtle sanctuary. With its white coral-sand beach, shallow reef and steep drop-off, it makes a great day trip that combines snorkeling with a short rest on the sand.
Mantigue Island is a small island about
3.5 km
off Camiguin's east coast in the Bohol Sea. It is also known as Magsaysay Island and belongs to the municipality of Mahinog. At only about 4 hectares, you can walk all the way around it in
15–20 minutes
. A fine white coral-sand beach rings the edge, and thick trees in the middle provide shade.

The island used to be a small fishing village. After the local government declared the area a sea turtle sanctuary and marine protected area, residents moved to the mainland, and nobody lives here now. The municipality of Mahinog looks after the island, and former residents make a living by taking part in the boats that carry visitors. In other words, the entrance and environmental fees you pay go toward protecting the island and supporting the local community.

One side of the island is a white-sand beach with a shallow reef, while the other side is a drop-off where the seabed suddenly plunges deep. On the shallow side, even beginners can see table corals and small tropical fish with just a mask and snorkel, and the deeper side offers a chance to meet larger fish and sea turtles. These are wild animals and cannot be seen every time, so it is best to keep your expectations modest.

Mantigue is not an island to stay overnight on but one to visit during the day. There are no restaurants or shops and the length of your stay is limited, so you only need to free up half a day in your Camiguin plans. If White Island is about volcano views from a sandbar, Mantigue is about a quiet beach and snorkeling. Most visitors do the two on separate days, or on the same day with one in the morning and the other in the afternoon.

The main beach where boats land combines fine white sand with clear water. Because the island is so small, walking along the beach brings you all the way around before you know it, so it is easy to find a good spot for photos.

The water in front of the beach is shallow and the coral is close, so even first-time snorkelers will feel at ease. You can rent a mask and snorkel at the departure point, and a separate snorkeling fee is collected on the island.

The far side of the island is a drop-off where the bottom falls away steeply. It is known for big table corals and larger fish such as barracuda and jackfish, which makes it popular with confident swimmers.

The island is a designated area for protecting sea turtles. Some visitors report meeting turtles while snorkeling, but there is no guarantee. If you do see one, keep your distance and never touch or chase it.
The middle of the island is thickly wooded, so it stays shady even at midday, and you can follow a path along the edge. A full lap takes about
15–20 minutes
, which makes it an easy stroll to cool off.
Small shaded huts by the beach can be used for a fee. The midday sun is strong, so it is worth planning a break in a hut or under a tree to have a snack.
For an extra fee, your boat driver will circle the island and take photos of you. You can see the island's forest and coral areas from an angle you cannot get from the beach.

children.text: Leave Mambajao and head to the Mantigue Island departure point in Mahinog. The ride takes about
30 minutes
At the tourist office at the departure point, pay the boat fare, entrance fee and environmental fee, and rent snorkeling gear.
Ride a bangka for about
20 minutes
to the island. Your time on the island starts now.
Snorkel in the shallow reef in front of the beach. Morning, when the fish are most active, is best.
Have some water and rest in a beach hut, then walk once around the island.
Take the boat back to the main island at the agreed time. Have lunch at a restaurant in Mahinog or Mambajao.
Agree on your return time with the boat driver beforehand. The stay on the island is said to be limited to about 3 hours at most, so check locally.
Have breakfast at your lodging and set out toward Mahinog by scooter or tricycle.
Complete the formalities at the Mantigue Island departure point and cross to the island.
Return from the island, then have lunch and rest.
Drive along the east and north coast road toward Mambajao and enjoy the villages and sea views.

Plans in Camiguin change easily with the weather. It is safest to check on the morning of your trip whether boats are running.

Many guides say there is no direct flight from Manila to Camiguin Airport (CGM). The most common way is to fly from Manila to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) near Cagayan de Oro, then continue by land and sea.

and costs about

If you start from Cebu, you can take Cebgo's direct flight to Camiguin Airport. Routes change, so confirm before booking.
To arrive in a single day from Manila, take a morning flight and reach Balingoan before the late-afternoon ferries.

3.5 km
away.
You hire a whole boat and fill it with passengers; the fare is quoted at about
(for 4 to 6 people). If your group is small, sharing with other travelers at the same time slot cuts the cost.

Camiguin lies between the Bohol Sea and the Mindanao Sea and can be visited all year, but March to June, when the sea is calm and visibility is good, is the best time for snorkeling. The weather is clear and the sun strong then, so you need sunscreen and a hat.

During the northeast monsoon from December to February, wind and waves can keep boats from sailing on some days, and from July to November, when the rainy season overlaps, sudden squalls can change your plans. In any season, check on the morning of your trip whether boats are running.

There are no restaurants, shops or lodging on the island, and it can only be visited during the day. Bring your own water, snacks and lunch, and take all your trash back with you. There may be small shops near the departure point, but choices are limited, so it is safest to buy supplies in Mambajao beforehand.

Most lodging is around Agoho and Yumbing beaches near Mambajao, with a few quiet beach resorts scattered around Mahinog. If you only plan to visit Mantigue, a place near Mahinog is convenient, but Mambajao has far more restaurants and transport. Most people either eat a good meal before heading to the island or have lunch afterward at a restaurant in Mahinog or Mambajao.
The stay on the island is said to be limited to about
3 hours
at most. Agree on your return time with the boat driver. One guide (2023) mentions about ₱100 per extra hour, so check locally.
Operating hours are generally known to be from
to
, and the last pickup can be early in the afternoon. Check the day's times at the departure point.
Bring water, snacks, a towel and a change of clothes. Nothing is sold on the island.
To protect the coral, use reef-safe sunscreen and do not step on or touch the coral while snorkeling.
There is little shade at midday, so going early in the morning is cooler and you will also see more fish.
A waterproof pouch or case keeps your belongings from getting wet on the boat.
Bring plenty of cash in small bills. Cards are often not accepted at the departure point or on the island.
Prices change often and differ slightly depending on who is quoting them. Check the latest announcements and keep your receipts from the office.
Sea turtles and corals are protected. Do not touch, feed or chase them, and follow your boat driver's judgment on days with strong currents or waves.
The drop-off side gets deep suddenly and may have currents. If you are not a strong swimmer, wear a life jacket.
On windy days or during typhoon season, boats may be canceled or withdraw early. Leave some slack in your schedule.
The midday UV is strong and there is a risk of sunburn and heatstroke. A hat and long-sleeved rash guard are recommended.
There are no medical facilities on the island. In an emergency you must come back to the main island by boat, so bring your own basic medicines.
Official fees and rules can change. Follow the guidance of the Mahinog tourism office at the departure point first.
A sandbar in the sea north of Camiguin, about
15 minutes
by boat. Together with Mantigue, it is one of the two main sea attractions in Camiguin.

children.text: A place where you can see an old cemetery that sank after a volcanic eruption and a cross standing in the sea, reachable along the coastal road toward Mambajao.
